featured_reviews.review_text:
I wish I could say my issues with this place were about the dancing, they're not. It's everything around it.
There's a real pattern here of staff and members being made to feel guilty for having a life outside the studio. Time off requests get met with pressure, not understanding. It starts to feel less like a class and more like an obligation you're not allowed to question.
The part that pushed me to actually write this review, though, is what happens after someone leaves. Instead of just letting people go their own way, there's a habit of rewriting the story afterward, bringing up private details with current students, looping in family members who had nothing to do with the original issue, and generally making sure the departing person looks like the problem.
None of this shows up on the Instagram page. It's all curated smiles and performance clips. But ask around a little before you sign up, because the gap between the public image and the internal culture is bigger than it should be.
Good instruction isn't worth much if the environment around it runs on control and guilt instead of respect.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I wasted 7,800 of my money at a recent class. They tell me the policy has been there for over 15 years; which quite frankly is archaic in today's day and age. How can someone lock someone into a class and not have the common courtesy to meet expectations. Maybe it's an India thing but small businesses really don't cater to the best interest of customers.

So here's what happened to me. I'm 41 and I signed up for the Intro Commercial Hip Hip class since I'm in town for only a month. There is no upfront transparency on the group dynamic or class structure of what to expect, nor any introductions. When I got to class, the majority (90%) of students were teenagers 9-15 (which is great) but not something I was expecting or looking for. In addition to that most are repeat students and it felt like I had a bigger learning curve. The teacher was really nice although I already voiced my concern (even before attending) that this is something I'm not interested in (or had in mind).

At this point, they lock me into taking the first class and needless to say, have communicated with me that I won't get any money back due to their "policy". So they just made 7,800INR from an NRI who was naive enough to sign up. Please don't make the same mistake.

I'm not here to make any establishment look bad. The studio space is beautiful. Dev Sir is great but I do think it's important for me to voice my opinion so folks like me who are interested know upfront what they are getting into.

Please ask for a TRIAL or else they will lock you into their class. It's unfortunate that these "rules" still exist but to me it seems like a distasteful means to meet the bottom line and make money.
